newsitem.title: UK: Halifax mulls returning excess cash - paper.
newsitem.headline: Halifax mulls returning excess cash - paper.

text.p: British building-society turned bank Halifax Plc will consider returning excess capital to shareholders unless it finds a clear way of earning them a better return, the Guardian said on Wednesday.
In an interview with the newspaper, Halifax chief executive Mike Blackburn said the bank was "sitting on a lot of surplus capital".
"The board is agreed we might be best advised to distribute to shareholders," the Guardian quoted Blackburn as saying.
Halifax has been widely tipped as a potential bidder for other financial services providers, with a cash pile of around 3.0 billion pounds ($5 billion) to fund any acquisitions.
The bank, which has a market capitalisation of nearly 20 billion pounds floated on the London Stock Exchange on June 20, giving its members hefty windfalls.

But the Guardian said Blackburn saw no virtue in moving from personal banking towards the commercial sector, the paper said. But there would still be the possibility of increasing the bank's regional coverage through acquisitions or "agency" deals and other outlets.
Halifax, Britain's largest mortgage lender, had steered clear of of the re-mortgage market where it believes mistakes have been made, the Guardian said. REUTER AS ($ = 0.599 British Pounds)
